title: console-latency-decomposition-whiteboard-notes
content:
Context:
This doc captures the whiteboard session (10/14) on decomposing latency signals for the Redwood Console UX. Goal: produce a compact, operator-friendly dashboard that maps end-to-end perceived latency to internal token-level and infra signals, with a clear sampling policy and low query cost.

High-level thesis / constraints:
- Operators care about perceived latency (time-to-first-token + time-between-chunks) more than raw p99 server-side numbers; console panels should reflect that.
- Dashboard must be cheap: prefer aggregated rollups + targeted trace links instead of high-cardinality raw traces.
- Tracing must preserve tenant privacy (strip PII) and not blow trace storage budgets.
- Signal mapping should allow quick drilldowns to: model fanout, routing fallbacks, kv-cache cold hits, and autoscaler events.

Proposed SLI decomposition (user-facing labels -> instrumentation mapping):
1) TTF(T) - Time to first token (client-observed) -> map to: gateway latency + model-invoke-first-token + prefetch serialization time. Primary metrics: client_ttf_ms (histogram), gateway-queue_ms, model-init_ms.
2) Chunk-pace (streaming cadence) -> tokens_per_second during stream window; derived from token_emit_intervals.
3) Cold-cache tail -> fraction of requests where kv_warmth_index < 0.3 and TTF spike > baseline. Metric: kv_warmth_ratio, kv_eviction_count.
4) Routing tail -> requests routed to lower-capacity tier or fallback variant. Metric: route_variant, fallback_rate.
5) Infra disruption events -> pod_restarts, preemption_rate, node_cpu_spike.

Dashboard layout sketch (panels prioritized top->bottom):
- Panel A: Perceived-latency funnel (line for TTF p50/p90/p99, streaming-latency p90) with quick toggles by model and region.
- Panel B: Attribution waterfall (aggregate: gateway | model-init | kv-warm | routing | network) for a selected spike window; each bar links to example traces.
- Panel C: Heatmap: token cadence vs request size (helps find slow-scaling large-context calls).
- Panel D: Top N traces sampler: shows 3 representative traces for each spike bucket (prefering traces with full token timestamps).
- Panel E: Cost lens: token-cost vs latency correlation scatter (detect expensive/slow tenants).

Trace sampling policy (draft):
- Lightweight sampling: sample 1% of all requests for full-span capture, biased to tail events (TTF > p95 or fallback_rate > 0.05).
- On spike detection: switch to burst mode for 5m -> 10% sampling for affected routes/models.
- Redaction: always strip request text, only capture token timing and anonymized token counts; store token hashes for correlation only (hashed with per-org salt).

Investigation playbook (operator steps):
1) Confirm perceived-latency spike on Panel A for tenant(s).
2) Use Panel B waterfall to identify dominant contributor.
3) If kv-warmth implicated -> check kv_eviction_rate and recent model loads; run prefresh probe via /internal/prefetch endpoint.
4) If routing implicated -> inspect rollout logs, check model-variant capacity metrics, and look for graceful-fallback markers.
5) If infra implicated -> check node metrics, recent preemptions and autoscaler events; open SRE runbook if pod_restart_rate > threshold.

Open questions & trade-offs (needs decisions):
- How much of the original request context can we keep in traces without violating privacy? Proposal: zero request text; capture only sanitized prompt hashes and a short intent-tag (operator-defined picklist).
- Sampling bias vs cost: aggressive tail sampling helps debugging but increases trace volume; need cost guardrails and auto-throttle.
- Panel interactivity: should waterfall compute be pre-aggregated or on-the-fly? Pre-agg reduces query costs but adds lag.
- Multi-tenant visibility: cross-tenant rollups are useful for platform ops but could leak behaviour patterns; ensure tenant scoping by default.

Short experiment plan (MVP, 3 sprints):
Sprint 0 (prototype):
- Implement client_ttf_ms histogram (gateway) + token_emit_interval instrumentation (model side).
- Add quick waterfall aggregator job that computes component percentiles for 1h windows.
Sprint 1 (console panels):
- Build Panel A and Panel B with drill-to-trace links.
- Implement basic sampling policy (1% global, bias to tails).
Sprint 2 (hardening):
- Add prefetch probe integration, heatmap panel, and cost-lens panel.
- Add auto-scaling hooks to mark scaling windows on dashboard.

Action items / owners:
- Implement gateway TTF metric: Marco Ruiz (ticket OBS-1184) - due 2025-11-05.
- Token emission timestamps in runtime: Aisha Patel (PR #402) - due 2025-11-12.
- Console panel prototype: Jonah Kim (frontend) - wireframe by 2025-11-20.
- Sampling policy infra: Eleanor Park + SRE pairing - design doc by 2025-11-28.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Try showing waterfall as stacked area and stacked bar in A/B to see operator preferences.
- Consider a microprobe that simulates long-context queries at low qps for kv-warmth experiments.
- Keep axis units consistent (ms vs seconds) and label "perceived" vs "server" latency.

References / related tickets:
- OBS-1184 (gateway TTF)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/402 (token timestamps)
- Confluence: Console telemetry primer (page id 987654321)

Status: draft. Next meeting 2025-12-03 to review sprint 0 telemetry samples and adjust sampling thresholds.
